Bill.BriefDescription: Authorizing utilities to engage in environmental mitigation efforts.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to authorizing utilities to engage in environmentalmitigation efforts; adding a new section to chapter 35.92 RCW; addinga new section to chapter 54.04 RCW; and creating a new section.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: The legislature finds and declares thatoffset contracts and other greenhouse gas mitigation efforts are arecognized utility purpose that confers a direct benefit on theutility's ratepayers. The legislature declares that this act isintended to reverse the result of Okeson v. City of Seattle (2007) byexpressly granting municipal-owned utilities and public utilitydistricts the statutory authority to engage in mitigation activities tooffset their utility's impact on the environment.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 35.92 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) A city or town authorized to acquire and operate utilities forthe purpose of furnishing the city or town and its inhabitants andother persons with electricity for lighting and other purposes may p. 1 HB 1929develop and make publicly available a plan for the utility to achieve nonet emissions from all sources of greenhouse gases it owns, leases,uses, contracts for, or otherwise controls. (2) A city or town authorized to acquire and operate utilities forthe purpose of furnishing the city or town and its inhabitants andother persons with electricity for lighting and other purposes may, aspart of its utility operation, mitigate the environmental impacts ofits operation and any power purchases, such as greenhouse gasemissions. The mitigation may include all greenhouse mitigationmechanisms recognized by independent, qualified organizations withproven experience in emissions mitigation activities. Mitigationmechanisms may include the purchase of carbon offsets. Any carbonoffset purchased after the effective date of this section must berecognized by any greenhouse gas registry developed by the state.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 54.04 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) A public utility district may develop and make publiclyavailable a plan for the district to achieve nonet emissions from allsources of greenhouse gases it owns, leases, uses, contracts for, orotherwise controls. (2) A public utility district may, as part of its utilityoperation, mitigate the environmental impacts of its operation and anypower purchases, such as greenhouse gas emissions. The mitigation mayinclude all greenhouse mitigation mechanisms recognized by independent,qualified organizations with proven experience in emissions mitigationactivities. Mitigation mechanisms may include the purchase of carbonoffsets. Any carbon offset purchased after the effective date of thissection must be recognized by any greenhouse gas registry developed bythe state.
